### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `54ecd3c294681b5f8eda1dae76c620af8127f850` — the merge of head `4e762e2a95fa3676d5f3ced3aed24ebe0a5cd0d4` into base `ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 54ecd3c294681b5f8eda1dae76c620af8127f850 && git checkout 54ecd3c294681b5f8eda1dae76c620af8127f850
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751 4e762e2a95fa3676d5f3ced3aed24ebe0a5cd0d4 && git checkout -B drift-repro ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751 && git merge --no-ff 4e762e2a95fa3676d5f3ced3aed24ebe0a5cd0d4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `337e86f47cc4e881268b1910d99cc18088aed86c`
Local-runs: none

Face: the declaration face alone (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset at this head). No `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path, so per `contract-review.md` the record is the lane seat's at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Inputs: card #28405 and claim, the os-dev-report 6552451120, and the source diff read whole at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`sys_automation_run.flow_checksum` (new nullable text column)**: right. Additive and optional; a row without it reads `undefined` (`readFlowChecksum`), which `resolveResumeTarget` treats as "no identity" and resumes on the armed definition, node checked, as before (card item 3). It is written beside the live suspension and beside a consumed-suspension snapshot, so a restore re-arms the pause pinned to the same body.
- **`SuspendedRun.flowChecksum?` (optional member on an exported type)**: right. Optional; every existing store and caller compiles and behaves as before.
- **`AutomationEngine.setFlowHistorySource` and the exported `FlowHistorySource` type**: right. Additive, the same shape as the existing `setPackagedFlowSource` / `PackagedFlowSource` pair. The plugin wires it to `SysMetadataRepository.getByHash` with `orgLabel: 'env'`, the label the protocol's own repository uses; a composition without a data engine or without `sys_metadata_history` answers `null`, never a throw.
- **Identity**: right. `hashSpec(body, 'flow')`, the checksum `sys_metadata_history` keys by; the dev measured the parked row's value equal to the history row the save wrote, on a real `saveMetaItem` over sqlite.
- **Resume order and the one classifier**: right. Armed-if-match, then the history, then a body this process registered; `unresumableSuspensionCause` (already `async`) and `resumeInternal` both go through the same `resolveResumeTarget`, so the pre-flight and the resume cannot disagree (item 5). A withdrawn flow is still `Flow '…' not found`.
- **Outage**: right. A history read that throws answers `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` and leaves the suspension unconsumed, the answer an unreadable suspended-run store already gives; it never falls through to the armed definition.
- **Unrecoverable pinned body (item 4, decided on the card)**: right. Resumes on the armed definition, node checked, with one `warn` naming flow, version and checksum. Never silent.
- **`resolveResumeTarget` becoming `async`**: not a surface change; it is not exported from the package index.
- **Nothing else moves**: no route, error code, metadata key or `packages/spec` path. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/service-automation` patch**: accepted, as on #28403 and #28418 for the same shape (optional members and a setter on a service package; the changeset gate passes it).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flow credentials** (#20790) stay keyed by flow name, node id and key against the live flow, so a run resumed on a pinned body reads the current credential at those positions. Recorded in the PR's acceptance notes; not owed here.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-oxn0ek`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QUs3BtyH9zgxKzYrJiH18J`

**VERDICT: PASS**

ACCEPT · PR #28500 · Head-sha `4e762e2a95fa3676d5f3ced3aed24ebe0a5cd0d4` · 2026-11-01T03:26Z

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 自动化运行暂停时记下所跑流程体的内容校验和（新增可空列 `sys_automation_run.flow_checksum`）；恢复时按它找回当时那一版：当前版本相同就用当前的，否则从元数据历史 `getByHash` 读，再不行用本进程注册过的版本。
- **为什么改：** 审批或屏幕步骤可能等好几天，期间流程重新发布，原来等待中的运行会跑到新定义上，节点改名时还会直接 `RUN_NOT_FOUND`。
- **风险与回滚：** 新运行仍从当前定义开始；旧行没有校验和时照旧读当前定义；找不回原版本时用当前定义并记 warn；历史库读不到时回 `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`，运行保持暂停可重试。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts` 的 `resolveResumeTarget`；`plugin.ts` 的 `flowHistoryReader`。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/flow-version-pinning.test.ts src/flow-version-pinning.integration.test.ts`。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位落地。

席位意见：预检和恢复仍走同一个判定，历史读失败不会退回当前定义，找不回时有 warn 不静默；可合。

## 席位核对

- **Form:** 15 files, +867/-26. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28500`: NOT governed, 893 lines ≤ 3000, Tier S. Declaration of record: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (the column, `SuspendedRun.flowChecksum?`, `setFlowHistorySource` and `FlowHistorySource`); TIER_DEFAULT review PASS at this head (6552699922; first record 6552473037 at `337e86f4`). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `@objectstack/service-automation` patch.
- **Premise measured:** the parked row's `flow_checksum` equals the `sys_metadata_history` checksum the save wrote (integration test over one sqlite file, two engine lifetimes, real `saveMetaItem`).
- **Gates (check-runs at the pinned head):** 48 runs: 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending; mergeable, clean. Dev: 62 derived, 61 run, 1 NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, needs a full build; CI runs it); `pnpm lint` 0; package 3115/3115 with typecheck; 8 ablations red, each restored.
- **CI fix at this head:** `337e86f4` was red on Test Core (4/8): `plugin-approvals` `deleted-flow-decision-refusal.test.ts` expected `RESUME_TARGET_LOST` after a republish removed the parked node, which this card changes on purpose. `4e762e2a` re-judges that one case (withdraw, then the node-less body); its assertions are unchanged; plugin-approvals 1366/1366.
- **Accepted deviations:** the thread ran at project default effort, not the xhigh asked. `getByHash` is reached through a `SysMetadataRepository` built in `plugin.ts` over the data engine, because the protocol keeps its repository private; no file outside the surface. Two old pins re-judged: a republish-renamed node now finishes on the pinned body; `RUN_NOT_FOUND` is kept for a truly unrecoverable body.
- **Out of scope and where it goes:** flow credentials (#20790) stay keyed against the live flow by name, node id and key; recorded in the PR's acceptance notes. N-11, N-18 and recording code bodies in history stay out, as the card says. `Skills-docs: none`.
- **Landing clause:** Tier S ordinary queue landing. The seat flips ready and enables auto-merge through the relay, then confirms MERGED and closes out #28405.
